svg.title: BugSigDB automated curation: logical view
svg.desc: A held-out gold is built from the public BugSigDB export. The curator takes a PMID, resolves the paper, reads its text, tables, figures and optionally supplements, segments it into experiments, finds the evidence for each, extracts and resolves taxa, and emits a validated prediction record with a sidecar. The scorer is the only reader of gold; human review sees drafts only. A data firewall separates the curator from the gold.
svg.text: What each part does and what it may read. Stage codes (S0–S10) are those of Table 2; Figure 2 maps the parts to commands.
A · CORPUS — build the held-out gold
+ PMID → PMCID map (84% of studies have PMC full text)
B · CURATE — input: a PMID, and nothing else
NCBI idconv; Europe PMC if throttled
tables and figures by p(DA), once per
study; one regex pick without Clef
↻ for each experiment stub (with Clef, up to 3 ranked artifacts are tried in turn)
taxa and direction from the first
split designs only: check each taxon
Services and sources the stages draw on
S5a · S1b screen · S4 body site
C · EVALUATE — the only reader of gold
all cut by gold source type
D · HUMAN REVIEW — a draft, never gold
one HTML page per draft, with its sidecar,
Names → taxids through the same TaxonomyDB;
retired ids are canonicalised on both sides.
Records cross the firewall one way: curator → scorer
and curator → reviewers. Gold never flows back.
data firewall: the curator never reads gold
